dossier_meta.statement_text: Do there exist $c, \varepsilon > 0$ with the following property? Let $\mathcal{B} = (B_1, B_2, B_3)$ be a blockade in a graph $G$, and let $W$ be its width. If there is no $\mathcal{B}$-transversal triangle, then there exist distinct $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $X \subseteq B_i$ and $Y \subseteq B_j$, such that $X, Y$ is a pure pair, and $|X|, |Y| \geq \varepsilon W^c$.
dossier_meta.context_text: This is a variant of a conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. Settling Question 1.3 was the authors' initial goal, though they were unable to do so. It is also equivalent to the $k=3$ case of Theorem 1.4 (which handles cycles of length $k \geq 4$), and can be reduced to the sparse case where every vertex in $B_i$ has at most $|B_j|/100$ neighbours in $B_j$ for all distinct $i, j \in \{1,2,3\}$.
